title: Differential pair + tail
description: The bare differential-pair transconductor sized by half-circuit: one input device, the tail source under it, and the diode-connected reference that biases the tail. Biased from the TAIL NODE and entered from the COMMON MODE, exactly like the 5T OTA: the pair's source sits at $V_{tail}$ (its body bias), its drain-source voltage is $V_{out} - V_{tail}$, and the tail device's drop IS the tail node — nothing iterated, no estimate to retune. The currents are stated the way the circuit sets them: only the bias reference is programmed, with $I_{tail}$; the tail device shares that reference's gate and width, so what it delivers is $I_{tail}$ less the mirror's drain-voltage error; and each side of the pair carries half of what the tail delivers. Held fixed and asked about at another process condition, the design therefore moves as the silicon would — one programmed current, with every other device following it through a shared gate or a shared node. The engine searches $V_{tail}$ in its range until the produced $CM_{in} = V_{tail} + V_{GS}$ equals the $CM_{dc}$ the application presents; sweep $CM_{dc}$ to trace the common-mode axis. The load is left abstract — a spec conductance gds_load_est (its inverse is the load resistance $R_L$) — so this sheet sizes the input stage independently of whatever mirror, resistor, or cascode terminates the drains. The common-mode gain and CMRR are estimate-grade (the tail output conductance sets them); a real CMRR also depends on drain-load and layout mismatch, so trust the sim for sign-off.

params.name: vn_target
params.note: input-referred thermal density budget (one side), set above the 23.1 nV/rtHz floor measured on a sky130 tt realization of this pair rather than above the gamma-model row — a budget that only clears the model is not a budget

params.name: vos_target
params.note: input offset budget, 1 sigma; a bare half-micron pair under a tail programmed to 20 uA sits near 7.6 mV with a generic Pelgrom coefficient

params.name: gds_load_est
params.note: conductance loading each drain; R_L = 1/gds_load_est. Set from the terminating load (mirror gds, resistor, or cascode)

params.name: CM_lo
params.note: input CM range, low edge — checked exactly by the cm-lo edge at every evaluation (the sweep put the widest closing range at 0.96-1.39 V on sky130 tt at the shipped choices). The edge checks the ENDPOINT; the interior is the sweep's to show

params.name: CM_hi
params.note: input CM range, high edge — its ENDPOINT checked by the cm-hi edge

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: the input common mode the application presents. The engine places the tail node so the sheet sits exactly here; sweep it to trace the common-mode axis

params.name: V_out_dc
params.note: drain DC level; sets the input device vds. Whatever terminates the drains sets it (a mirror diode drop, a resistor drop, a folded-cascode source), and that load is not on this sheet: only its conductance, gds_load_est, is

params.name: V_tail
params.note: the tail node — the one free bias variable, solved rather than set: the engine searches between min and max (the range it is searched in, not slider bounds) until the produced common mode equals CM_dc. The shown value is where it landed

params.name: I_tail
params.note: the current the bias reference is programmed to — the one current on this sheet that is typed. The tail device mirrors it 1:1 through the shared gate and delivers it less the mirror's drain-voltage error (the tail node normally sits below the reference's diode drop); slew rate, bandwidth and supply current are computed from what is delivered, not from this number

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion: sets gm per current, noise, and the CM-low edge

params.name: gm_id_tail
params.note: inversion level of the bias reference, which the tail device inherits through the shared gate: higher V* costs CM-low headroom but tightens the current source

params.name: L_tail
params.note: length of the bias reference and of the tail device, which mirror at one length: longer shrinks the mirror's drain-voltage error and lifts the common-mode rejection

doc.title: Tail bias reference
doc.description: The diode-connected reference the programmed current $I_{tail}$ flows into — the one device on this sheet whose current is typed. Its drain is its gate, so its $V_{DS}$ is its own $V_{GS}$ and the table is read along that diagonal with nothing estimated. It publishes its width and its gate voltage, which is all the tail device needs to copy it.

doc.title: Tail current source
doc.description: The tail device, on the bias reference's gate at the reference's width: a 1:1 mirror of the programmed current, with the tail node as its drain-source voltage. Its current is read off the table rather than typed — the reference sits at its own diode drop and this device at $V_{tail}$, so it delivers the programmed current scaled by what that difference in $V_{DS}$ does through its $g_{ds}$. Its saturation headroom sets the CM-low edge, and its output conductance sets the common-mode rejection.

params.name: W_t
params.note: the bias reference's width — a 1:1 copy

params.name: vgs_t
params.note: the bias reference's gate voltage — the gate wire the two share

doc.title: Input-pair device
doc.description: Half-circuit input device carrying half of what the tail device delivers. Its source sits at the tail node — that is its body bias — and its drain at V_out_dc, so its drain-source voltage is what is left between them.

equations.name: CM_in
equations.note: the input common mode this bias produces — an OUTPUT here, not a setting; rises monotonically with the tail node, so the pin is a well-posed one-unknown search

equations.name: Gm
equations.note: differential-pair transconductance is the half-circuit gm

equations.name: Rout
equations.note: the resistance this stage presents at its output: the input device's own output conductance in parallel with the estimated load conductance. The gain assumes a capacitive load, so nothing here models a resistive one; this row is what a composing parent checks its own loading against

equations.name: Av
equations.note: half-circuit gain into the device gds in parallel with the load conductance

equations.name: SR
equations.note: the whole tail current steered into the load — the current the tail device delivers, not the number the reference is programmed to

equations.name: vn_in
equations.note: input-referred thermal density of the pair (both devices, hence the sqrt(2)); add the load's own contribution per the terminating device

equations.name: vos
equations.note: input-pair Pelgrom offset; the load pair adds in quadrature once its geometry is known

equations.name: Acm
equations.note: estimate: common-mode gain magnitude, set by the tail output conductance splitting between the two halves

equations.name: CMRR
equations.note: estimate: differential gain over common-mode gain; a real CMRR also depends on load and layout mismatch, so trust the sim

equations.name: tail_headroom
equations.note: how far the tail node sits above the tail device's saturation edge — exact, because the tail node is the variable rather than something inferred from a common mode

equations.name: cgg_in
equations.note: estimate: the capacitance one input terminal presents — the gate capacitance of a single input device. Gate capacitance only, because the Miller term needs the gate-drain fraction and these tables do not carry it, so a driving stage sees more than this. No rule reads it

equations.name: I_q
equations.note: estimate: quiescent supply current of the stage — the current the tail device delivers is the only branch these rows model, since the load is entered as a conductance rather than sized as a branch. The reference branch that programs it is shared bias infrastructure, typically one reference feeding several stages, and is not counted here. The datasheet line for comparing designs; no rule reads it

checks.note: reads each device's thermal noise from the table where the table carries it, and the gamma = 1 estimate where it does not; it stays advisory because a sheet cannot know which table it will be evaluated on, and the simulator owns noise sign-off
the common mode this bias produces has to sit inside the range the application presents
paired with cm-not-below. Sweep CM_dc to see the whole span that closes
trips when the tail node is pushed so high the pair runs out of drain-source voltage at the drain DC level
estimate: a longer tail L (lower tail gds) lifts CMRR; sim owns the real number

operatingRange.name: cm-lo
operatingRange.note: the claimed low edge, checked exactly: the sheet re-evaluates at CM_dc = CM_lo on the design this run produced, with its own tail-node solve. Replaces the linearized reach estimate

operatingRange.name: cm-hi
operatingRange.note: the claimed high edge, checked the same way; the CM_dc sweep remains the authority on the full landscape
